Cold long-context comparison on Apple M3 Ultra
(same quantization on both models: UD-Q4_K_XL)

Qwen3.5-122B-A10B
- 2k:    prefill  940.74 tok/s, decode  43.97 tok/s
- 128k:  prefill  275.19 tok/s, decode  25.55 tok/s

NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B
- 2k:    prefill  598.70 tok/s, decode  34.20 tok/s
- 128k:  prefill  482.38 tok/s, decode  31.08 tok/s

2k -> 128k drop:
- Qwen3.5:   prefill -70.7%, decode -41.9%
- Nemotron:  prefill -19.4%, decode  -9.1%

Qwen is faster at 2k.
Nemotron preserves long-context throughput much better at 128k, with a large prefill advantage and a clear decode advantage.

Test profile (llama.cpp):
--parallel 1
--no-cont-batching
--cache-prompt
--cache-ram -1
--flash-attn on
--cache-type-k f16
--cache-type-v f16
--batch-size 2048
--ubatch-size 1024
--no-context-shift
